LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 9.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: My Friends Suggested vocabulary kind, caring, loving, funny, friendly, close, pl
Topic 9.1: Listening and speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of My Friends Suggested vocabulary kind, caring, loving, funny, friendly, close, pl in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly? 2. How can we improve our pronunciation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: learning independently is enhanced as they get motivated to perfect the pronunciation of various sounds.

• Digital literacy: learner’s ability to interact with technology is enhanced as they listen to an audio recording and mimics the sounds.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as learners collaborate with others as they sing and recite poems related to friends.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Self-awareness is nurtured as learners acquire knowledge about their friends.

Link to other Learning Areas

Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities as learners pronounce words with the target sounds correctly.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Audio recordings, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners,

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
